title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page has two unrelated blocks of scratch computation.

(1) Top half: fixing the composition-law convention for the 'path' description of an extension 1 -> pi -> E -> G -> 1. A group G acts on a (simply connected or path-groupoid) space X with base point a, and pi is the fundamental group of the base. E is the set of pairs (gamma, l) with gamma in G and l a homotopy class of paths.
- First convention: l runs from a to gamma^{-1}(a). The product is (gamma,l)(gamma',l') = (gamma gamma', gamma'^{-1}(l) o l'). Grothendieck checks this with a picture: a -> gamma'^{-1}a via l', then gamma'^{-1}a -> gamma'^{-1}gamma^{-1}a = (gamma gamma')^{-1}a via gamma'^{-1}(l).
- He rewrites this multiplicatively as (gamma.l)(gamma'.l') = (gamma gamma') (gamma'^{-1} l gamma') l'.
- He then switches to paths l : gamma(a) -> a. After a false start (gamma(l') o l', struck out), he gets l o gamma(l'). Putting the path first, he boxes the semidirect-product-like law (l,gamma)(l',gamma') = (l.gamma(l'), gamma gamma').
This is the standard description of the fundamental group of a homotopy quotient (orbifold or stack X//G), i.e. the extension of the 'modular' group G by pi. In the Teichmüller context this is presumably pi_1 of a moduli stack as an extension of a mapping-class or Teichmüller group. The isolated word u~ v~ u~^{-1} v~^{-1} (a commutator of lifts) suggests he wants lifts of generators to such an extension, e.g. lifting a genus-one commutator relation.

(2) Bottom half: computation in a central extension with central elements written zeta(n).
- Setup: alpha = u a^{-1} eps_3(tau'), beta = u b^{-1}. An attempted change of variables is struck out.
- He defines eta~ = beta~ sigma~(beta~)^{-1} = eta_0 zeta(6 nu), with sigma~ acting.
- Then sigma~(eta~) = sigma~(beta~) beta~^{-1} = eta~^{-1}, while also sigma~(eta~) = sigma~(eta_0) zeta(6 nu) = eta_0^{-1} zeta(6 nu).
- Conclusion: sigma~^2 commutes with beta~ only if nu_2 = 0, i.e. nu = 2nu'. So the 2-primary part of a parameter nu (apparently in Z/6, split as nu_2, nu_3) must vanish.
- Second attempt: eta~ = eta_0 = [beta_0, sigma_0] = u(sigma_0) sigma_0^{-1}, with sigma~ = sigma_0 zeta(3). Expanding gives eta~ = u(sigma_0) sigma_0^{-1} zeta(3(mu-1)), possibly normalised by 6nu (the denominator is hard to read).
- Final line: beta(sigma~) = u(sigma~), with beta(sigma~) = beta(sigma_0) zeta(3).
This is bookkeeping of central 'defects' when lifting an order-2 type element sigma and its conjugates to a central extension. The orders 2, 3, 6 and zeta(3), zeta(6nu) are reminiscent of SL2(Z)/B3-type central extensions and the Z/12, Z/6 abelianisations. The next page continues with u~(xi~_0) = xi(nu'-nu''-2nu) xi~_0 and congruence conditions in nu_2, nu_3, nu_6.
The purpose is likely deciding which lifts or normalisations (of a Galois or automorphism action on the Teichmüller tower, or of torsion elements) are compatible. This is a step in the Teichmüller-tower / Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type relation computations, but too fragmentary to pin down.
errors: The first attempt at the second convention (gamma(l') o l') is wrong and is corrected on the page to l o gamma(l'). The boxed formula (l,gamma)(l',gamma') = (l.gamma(l'), gamma gamma') is correct for paths l : gamma(a) -> a, composed left to right as 'l then gamma(l')' read appropriately.

In the last eta~ computation, the passage from zeta(3mu) sigma_0^{-1} zeta(-3) to zeta(3(mu-1)) uses that zeta is central. The '/6nu' in the exponent is unclear and may be a normalisation or a misreading; it cannot be verified.
The bottom computations are inconclusive scratch work: some lines are struck through and the final line is unfinished.

ideas.what: Description of the extension 1->pi->E->G->1 (fundamental group of a homotopy quotient) by pairs (group element, path from a to its translate), with explicit group law
ideas.modern_name: orbifold / stack fundamental group of X//G; path description of pi_1 of the homotopy quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Armstrong, Haefliger, Thurston for orbifolds; SGA1 for the étale version)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (exact sequence of fundamental groups for quotients and Galois actions); the 'Teichmüller groupoid' philosophy of Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Conditions for lifts of an involution-like element sigma to commute (up to central zeta terms) with a lifted element beta in a central extension, giving a parity condition nu_2 = 0
ideas.modern_name: computation of central obstructions/cocycles for lifting torsion elements to central extensions (SL2(Z)/B3-type)

deep.surprise_reason: The top half is a standard convention check for pi_1 of a homotopy quotient. The bottom half is fragmentary central-extension bookkeeping whose precise context cannot be reconstructed, and no new result is visible.
transcription_corrections: The phrase under the eta~ computation reads approximately 'sigma~^2 ne commute à beta~ que si nu_2 = 0 i.e. nu = 2nu'' ('sigma~^2 commutes with beta~ only if…'), not 'un commutati[?]'.
In the second-convention formula the struck-out term is gamma(l') o l'; the correction is l o gamma(l').
In the diagram, the struck-through label near gamma'(a) is gamma'(l') or gamma'(l) and is cancelled.
The final line probably reads 'beta(sigma~) = u(sigma~)' with 'beta(sigma_0) zeta(3)' beneath the left side; the symbol under the right side is unclear (possibly 'u' or 'i'), not necessarily iota.
The central elements are written as a script z (zeta); the next page writes similar symbols that the transcription renders as xi, which may be the same letter.
